Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

**About Apylon And The Opportunity

**Apylon is building agents for the most complex workflow out there - financial admin in healthcare.

Hospitals and payers move billions of euros through fragmented, manual workflows shaped by clinical data, payer rules, contracts, and local coding systems. We believe this is a data, machine-learning, and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

We are live with leading private hospitals and expanding quickly. Every hospital presents a different challenge: EHR systems are configured differently, national coding rules vary, and contracts describe the same clinical event in different terms. Your job is to help us turn that complexity into a system that learns: each new integration should make the next one faster, safer, and less expensive.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe. You’ll join the first small engineering team, with massive ownership over both what we build and how we build it.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

You’ll be responsible for

• Own EHR integrations end to end: APIs, schemas, undocumented behaviour, operational failure modes, and vendor changes.

• Build reusable integration-platform primitives for extraction, normalisation, versioning, replay, monitoring, and observability.

• Design the canonical data model that connects heterogeneous EHR data, reimbursement systems, national coding standards, and hospital-specific conventions.

• Build reliable inputs for our billing agents, including the constraints, validation, and evaluation systems that make model-assisted decisions safe to use in production.

• Work directly with hospital IT teams and EHR vendors: technical discovery, implementation, joint debugging, and onboarding.

• Take responsibility for the full lifecycle of your work: design, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and iteration from real-world data.

Who you are

• 3+ years building and operating production systems in complex, messy domains. We care more about demonstrated judgment and ownership than an exact number of years.

• Experience using LLMs as production components—not just developer tools. You understand when to use models, when deterministic systems are better, how to constrain outputs, and how to evaluate reliability.

• Strong data-modelling instincts. You know when abstraction creates leverage and when it hides important real-world variation.

• Comfort working from incomplete information. You form hypotheses, test them against data, and distinguish unknowns that can wait from assumptions that could invalidate the system.

• Confidence in customer-facing technical work: discovery calls, debugging sessions, and direct conversations with vendors and hospital IT teams.

• Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

• A practical, hands-on approach: equally comfortable designing an integration architecture and writing a quick script to answer an urgent question.

This role may be a strong fit if

You enjoy reverse-engineering systems you do not control, finding structure in messy real-world data, and turning one-off discoveries into reusable software. You are comfortable being the engineer in the room with customers and partners.

What this role is not

• Consulting or bespoke delivery work. Each integration must improve the product and reduce the marginal cost of the next.

• A role insulated from customers or operational reality.

• Pure platform engineering or pure integration work: the value comes from doing both.

• A role where incorrect mappings are merely technical defects. In this domain, they can produce incorrect invoices.

Bonus points

• Experience with healthcare interoperability or coding standards, including HL7v2, FHIR, or national messaging and reimbursement standards.

• Experience building and operating third-party integrations at scale.

• Experience in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated environment.

• Experience in an early-stage or fast-growing company.

• Working proficiency in Danish, or German.

Our tech stack

• Python

• Django

• React

• PostgreSQL

• AWS

• K8s

• Terraform

• Bedrock

• We’re pragmatic. You’ll have a big say in how it evolves.

What Apylon offers

• The chance to solve one of Europe’s biggest healthcare inefficiencies.

• Competitive salary + stock options (you’ll own part of what you build).

• 25 days of annual leave + local public holidays.

• Lunch on us during workdays at the office.

• Regular off-sites and social events. We like building together, not just working together.

• Travel within the EU roughly monthly. Onboarding a hospital, working through an integration with a vendor’s engineers, or spending time on-site to understand how the data is actually produced. If travelling to a hospital basement to figure out why an export is malformed sounds like a bad week, this isn’t your role.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code, powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue systems.

How to apply. If you're excited by the challenge of building intelligent, high-impact systems at the core of European healthcare and enjoy shipping fast, we'd love to hear from you.

**Nicolò Calcavecchia

jobs.description:
PhD Project in Muscular signaling and metabolism

  Nutrition Exercise and Sports (NEXS), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The August Krogh Section for Human and Molecular Physiology at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in “Elucidating the role of AMPK in Skeletal Muscular signaling and metabolism”. The project is part of the research project “Illuminating the signaling architecture of skeletal muscle insulin resistance”, which is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  By the use of phophosproteomics in human skeletal muscle, we recently discovered a novel phosphorylation site on AMPK alpha2 subunit regulated by mTORC1. This phosphorylation is associate with glucose uptake. We now wish to explore the relationship between the catabolic signal from AMPK and the anabolic signal from mTORC1 and the potential causal link to metabolic regulation. The project will primarily be conducted in mice by the use of transgenic KI models.

  Who are we looking for?

  We welcome applications from candidates with a strong academic background in physiology, biology, biomedical sciences, exercise science or a related field, and an interest in skeletal muscle physiology and metabolic regulation.

  The project combines animal studies with molecular and metabolic analyses. Experience in one or more relevant areas is an advantage, but applicants are not expected to have all of the skills already. Relevant experience could include in vivo or ex vivo research, metabolic phenotyping, muscle physiology, tissue processing, immunoblotting, immunoprecipitation or tracer-based assays.

  An interest in molecular signalling pathways involved in metabolism, including AMPK and nutrient sensing, would be valuable. Above all, we are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who is keen to learn and develop within a collaborative research environment.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?

  The group is a part of Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the Faculty of Scince, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and animal facilities.

  Our group work focuses on the molecular mechanisms through which physical activity promotes metabolic health.

  We are particularly interested in the intracellular interactions between exercise-induced signaling events and those triggered by insulin, aiming to unravel how a single bout of exercise can enhance muscle insulin sensitivity. Central to these studies is the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and its interacting partners, including mTOR and TBC1D4.

  We are studying this in humans using various cell/animal models for validation and mechanistic analyses.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Jørgen Wojtaszewski (NEXS, JW@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28751625) and Associate professor Rasmus Kjøbsted (NEXS, Rasmus.Kjobsted@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28344370)

   

  The PhD programme

 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have cand. med. (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 180 ECTS/3 FTE MSc). For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme)    	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Diploma allowing independent work with experimental animals 	
• Experiences with experimental animal work 	
• Experiences with experimental animal work related to metabolism and cellular signaling 	
• Experiences with experimental animal work related to skeletal muscle 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in muscle metabolism and cellular signaling 	
• Good English language skills   ***************************************************************************

  Application and Assessment Procedure

   Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 6 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Human Skin Biology and Wound Healing

  Department of Biology, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Biology at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a postdoctoral researcher in human skin biology and wound healing. The position is part of a newly established research group investigating how cells coordinate their behaviour to maintain and repair tissues.

  The position is fully funded for at least 2 years, with the possibility of extension, through generous funding from the LEO Foundation. The earliest possible start date is 1 April 2027. Please clearly state your availability and preferred start date in your cover letter.

  Information about the Department of Biology is available at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/. Information about the specific research section you will be affiliated with is available at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/research/cbp/.

  Project overview

  The overarching aim is to develop strategies to help people with slow- or non-healing wounds.

  This project investigates how planar cell polarity (PCP)—the coordinated orientation of cells within a tissue—contributes to human skin organization and wound repair. Although PCP signaling is essential for tissue organization across many organisms, its role in human epidermis remains poorly understood.

  You will establish reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) as an experimental model to investigate PCP signaling in human skin, then use advanced fluorescence microscopy to characterize PCP clusters, their polarization, and how they change during wound repair and in response to other stressors.

  The project bridges fundamental questions in cell and developmental biology with potential long-term applications in regenerative medicine and skin repair. It is supported by collaborators with expertise in RHE development and by access to confocal and advanced microscopy, including SIM, TIRF, and STED.

  The project provides a clear starting point and room to shape the research questions as findings emerge. In your cover letter, please clearly describe what interests you about the project and what related research questions you would be excited to explore.

  Your role

  We are seeking a motivated, technically skilled, and scientifically independent postdoctoral researcher to play a central role in establishing this research programme. As one of the first members of a newly established research group, you will have an exceptional opportunity to shape its experimental approaches, contribute to its scientific direction, and help build a collaborative, ambitious research environment.

  Your primary responsibility will be to establish and optimize experimental systems to investigate PCP signaling in reconstructed human epidermis. You will work closely with the PI while taking substantial ownership of day-to-day experimental development and execution of the project.

  Your responsibilities will include:

   	
• Establish and optimize robust, reproducible assays with mature, stratified RHE cultures. 	
• Develop and optimize immunostaining, advanced microscopy, and quantitative imaging workflows. 	
• Analyze and interpret experimental data, contributing scientific ideas, and identifying promising new research directions. 	
• Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at local and international conferences. 	
• Contribute to the development of a supportive, collaborative, and scientifically rigorous lab environment. 	
• Help train and supervise students or other researchers as the group expands.   Profile 

  We are seeking a curious and proactive researcher who can take ownership of their experiments while collaborating constructively with the project team. You do not need experience with every method listed below; training and collaboration will help you develop the techniques needed for the project.

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• PhD in cell biology, developmental biology, skin biology, molecular biology, tissue engineering, biophysics, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. 	
• Extensive hands-on experience in mammalian cell culture, with demonstrated ability to independently establish, optimize, and troubleshoot experimental protocols. 	
• Demonstrated experience in fluorescence microscopy and immunofluorescence staining. 	
• Evidence of scientific independence, initiative, and the ability to advance an experimental research project, including strong organizational skills. 	
• A solid publication record appropriate for your career stage. 	
• Excellent written and spoken English skills.   In the cover letter, you are encouraged to highlight an example of experimental independence, including situations in which you have established or substantially improved an experimental method, solved a challenging technical problem, or independently advanced a research project.

  Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with human keratinocyte culture, reconstructed human epidermis, organotypic skin cultures, or other 3D epithelial models. 	
• Experience establishing new experimental model systems or developing and optimizing complex cell-culture protocols. 	
• Experience with quantitative image analysis using Fiji/ImageJ, Python, or other comparable computational tools. 	
• Experience with molecular perturbation techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9, RNA interference, and genetic manipulation of mammalian cells. 	
• Experience with confocal microscopy or an advanced imaging technique such as SIM, TIRF, or STED. 	
• Experience mentoring or supervising students or junior researchers.   Research shows that women and other underrepresented groups often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. If you are excited about this position and believe you can contribute, we strongly encourage you to apply, even if your experience does not perfectly match every point. We value curiosity, motivation, and the potential and willingness to learn.

  What we offer

   	
• An opportunity to join a newly established research group and meaningfully contribute to its scientific development. 	
• A central role in an ambitious, externally funded research project that addresses fundamental and medically relevant questions. 	
• Substantial scientific independence and opportunities to develop novel experimental approaches. 	
• Close scientific interaction with the PI and opportunities to shape future research directions. 	
• Access to the research infrastructure and collaborative environment at the University of Copenhagen. 	
• Opportunities for international collaboration, conference participation, publication, and professional development.   The position offers an excellent opportunity for a researcher seeking to develop greater scientific independence and strengthen their qualifications for a future academic or research leadership career.

  Terms of employment

  The average weekly working hours are 37 hours.

  The place of employment is at the Department of Biology, Section for Cell Biology and Physiology, University of Copenhagen.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020. 

  Questions
 For further information, please contact PI: Silas Boye Nissen; boye.nissen@bio.ku.dk.

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, and other skills/experience relevant for the position (see above). 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.

  About us

  The newly established Friesen lab aims to understand, treat and prevent metabolic disease. We want to explore how a cell transitions from a healthy state to insulin resistance to type 2 diabetes and to reverse this process. Our group leverages human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived in vitro disease models that accurately represent the in vivo cell state. We study the molecular underpinnings of metabolism and insulin signaling in a variety of cell types, improving in vitro hPSC-derived metabolic disease models, and applying these for translational research.

  Your tasks will include designing experimental strategies, executing wet lab biology experiments, data analysis, and scientific writing and presentation. Additional tasks could include contributing to grant applications, and research-based supervision of MSc or PhD students.

jobs.description:
If you’re energised by turning complex process models into practical engineering decisions and thrive on solving challenging engineering questions through simulation, we’d love to hear from you!

**Who We Are

**We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

**About The Role

**We are looking for a Simulation Engineer with industrial experience to join our team of simulation specialists in Early Simulation Insights. As a team, we develop data-driven process models that support the design and optimisation of future API manufacturing facilities.

Your contribution will be important in transforming simulation results into practical engineering decisions that support facility design, capacity planning and utility-system configuration. Working closely with process, utility and modelling specialists, you will evaluate production scenarios, equipment requirements and operational strategies through dynamic simulations.

By testing assumptions and comparing alternatives early in the design process, you will help teams identify constraints, validate solutions and make informed decisions. In addition, you will contribute to the development of the department’s capabilities, methods and ways of working.

Location Denmark - Virum

Experience Minimum 3 Years

Department Early Simulation Insights

**How You Might Spend Your Days

**As a Simulation Engineer you’ll be:

• Building process models to evaluate capacity, utilisation and production schedules

• Assessing equipment configurations, batch strategies and cleaning approaches

• Modelling utility demand to support early facility and utility-system design

• Developing digital twins for early design verification and Virtual C&Q

• Translating simulation results into engineering recommendations with cross-functional specialists

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Curious and motivated to build new knowledge and explore complex engineering questions

• Structured in your approach and able to transform complexity into clear analyses and recommendations

• Open-minded and solution-oriented, with an interest in developing new methods and ways of working

• Comfortable taking ownership while collaborating across teams, disciplines and stakeholders

• Interested in understanding customer needs and translating technical insights into practical value

**What You Bring To The Role

**In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• You hold an MSc or PhD in Chemical Engineering, Process Systems Engineering, Simulation or a related discipline

• You have 3-5 years of experience with process modelling or simulation in pharma, biotech or another process industry

• You have hands-on experience with tools such as INOSIM, Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, MATLAB, Python, DWSIM or similar software

• You have a strong understanding of chemical engineering principles and can apply data-driven insights to engineering decision-making

• You are fluent in written and spoken English

Dalux continues to grow rapidly, and AI is creating entirely new possibilities for how construction professionals find information, understand complex project data, automate repetitive work, and make decisions.

We're looking for an AI Product Manager to help turn those possibilities into products that create real value for our users.

As an AI Product Manager at Dalux, you'll operate at the intersection of customer needs, rapidly evolving AI technology, and business strategy. You'll work closely with Product Design, AI engineers, developers, and other Product Managers to identify where AI can meaningfully improve construction workflows – and equally importantly, where it cannot.

Building AI products is different from traditional software development. Outputs are probabilistic, quality needs continuous evaluation, and product decisions involve trade-offs between accuracy, latency, cost, scalability, and user trust.

You'll help us navigate those trade-offs and establish how we build great AI products at Dalux.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• AI Product Discovery: Identify and validate problems where AI can create meaningful value rather than applying AI for its own sake.

• Customer Insights: Work closely with users and internal domain experts to understand construction workflows and identify opportunities for AI-powered improvements.

• Evaluation & Quality: Define what "good" looks like for AI features and establish evals, quality metrics, test cases, and feedback loops.

• AI Safety & Trust: Consider hallucinations, uncertainty, guardrails, failure modes, explainability, and user trust throughout product development.

• Feature Ownership: Lead AI-powered features from early experimentation and prototyping through delivery, evaluation, and continuous improvement.

• Technical Collaboration: Work closely with AI engineers and developers on model capabilities, context, architecture, latency, scalability, and cost.

• AI Product Strategy: Follow developments in models and AI technology and help determine which technological advances create meaningful opportunities for Dalux.

**About You

**We are looking for someone who combines strong product thinking with a solid understanding of modern AI.

You don't need to be an AI engineer, but you need enough technical understanding to make informed product decisions and have meaningful discussions with the engineers building these systems.

We believe you:

• Have experience building or managing customer-facing AI/ML products.

• Understand concepts such as LLMs, RAG, embeddings, context, agents, evals, and guardrails.

• Understand the fundamental difference between building deterministic software and probabilistic AI experiences.

• Can translate rapidly evolving technical capabilities into valuable user experiences.

• Are comfortable defining and measuring quality where traditional acceptance criteria are insufficient.

• Think critically about when AI is – and isn't – the right solution.

• Can balance user value, model quality, latency, scalability, and cost.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Experience with B2B SaaS is an advantage.

Experience with construction technology is welcome but not required. We have deep construction expertise within Dalux – for this role, we are particularly interested in adding strong AI product expertise to our organization.

**What To Expect At Dalux

**At Dalux, you'll join a product-driven company where ideas quickly become reality and where you'll have a direct impact on the products we build.

We offer:

• A collaborative and informal work environment with flat hierarchies

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives

• Talented and dedicated colleagues in an international team

• A central Copenhagen office, flexible work hours, and no dress code

• Monthly social events and an active community

• Attractive benefits including health insurance, lunch, fitness facilities, and free parking

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

**We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your resume and application as soon as possible.

**Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics.
